goal: A condenser microphone streaming kit on a boom arm and mini tripod, connected to a phone or computer through a sound card and cables.

steps.instruction: Insert the post at the bottom of the boom arm into the hole on top of the desk clamp and tighten it.
steps.why: The desk clamp photo shows a round hole on top and a locking knob on the side; the post at the bottom of the arm matches its width, and the manual lists the folding arm and clamp together as the support set.

steps.instruction: Screw the mic clip onto the top of the mini tripod.
steps.why: The tripod has a threaded post in the center of its top, and one end of the mic clip has a matching threaded socket; the small clip sits on the small stand as a desktop backup holder.

steps.instruction: Screw the small adapter onto the threaded tip at the front of the boom arm.
steps.why: The front of the arm has a protruding threaded tip and the adapter has a threaded hole underneath of the same size; it converts the thread for the mount.

steps.instruction: Screw the shock mount onto the top of the small adapter.
steps.why: The end of the shock mount's handle has a threaded hole and the adapter has a threaded stud on top; the mount is about twice the adapter's width, going from small to large to carry the mic.

steps.instruction: Insert the condenser mic into the center of the shock mount from above.
steps.why: The center of the shock mount is a hollow ring that matches the mic's diameter; the cylindrical mic is held by the elastic cords, which isolates vibration.

steps.instruction: Pull the foam cover over the mesh grille at the top of the mic.
steps.why: The soft foam cover's opening matches the mic's silver grille, and the manual lists the foam as fitting directly over the microphone.

steps.instruction: Clamp the pop filter's end clip onto the tube of the boom arm.
steps.why: The end of the pop filter's gooseneck has a clip with a knob whose opening fits the arm's tube; the gooseneck can position the screen in front of the mic.

steps.instruction: Plug the XLR end of the mic cable into the bottom of the mic.
steps.why: The bottom of the mic has a round pin socket, and one end of the black cable is the matching three-pin silver XLR connector.

steps.instruction: Connect the 3.5 mm end of the cable to the mic input on the sound card.
steps.why: The sound card has several 3.5 mm jacks on its side and the other end of the cable is a 3.5 mm plug; the sound card collects the signals.

steps.instruction: Plug one end of a white cable into the matching jack on the sound card.
steps.why: The white cables have 3.5 mm plugs that match the sound card's round jacks, and the manual uses these cables to connect a phone and the LIVE ports.

steps.instruction: Connect the USB audio adapter to the white cable, and plug the USB end into the computer.
steps.why: The white adapter shows two labeled jacks that fit the 3.5 mm plug of the white cable, and the manual describes it as the USB-to-audio adapter for computers.
